why: Interview fan-out is genuinely multi-agent: five conversations at once is a demo no single-agent tool can fake. The wedge is real respondents, and the room is full of them. Most teams will interview synthetic personas and lose the track's core: real beats staged.
need: Manager decomposes the research question into a screener and a discussion guide
Recruiter agent screens volunteers from the room and online via the messaging gateway
Interviewer subagents run 10 minute structured interviews in parallel with probing follow-ups
ElevenLabs voice option so interviews feel human, not like a form
Analyst codes transcripts into themes and every claim links to a verbatim quote
Writer publishes the findings report to Cloudflare Pages with method and sample disclosed
Run log and respondent profiles in Convex: who interviewed whom, when, and the handoffs
levelups: Remembers you: respondent profiles persist, a person from study one gets a shorter screener for study two. L4: the recruiter reuses known respondents unprompted. L5: wipe it and the panel is gone.

Learns from use: interviews that die early reshape the discussion guide. L4: drop-off and probe-success data retune questions between interviews. L5: show interview 1 vs interview 10 completion depth.

name: Podcast Clips Agency
build: Drop a podcast episode and an agent crew ships it: a transcriber, a moment scorer, parallel clip cutters, a captioner, a thumbnail artist, and a publisher that posts the top clips to the show's real social accounts.
hermes: A manager runs the pipeline with fan-out clip cutters, an in-crew judge panel scores hooks before anything ships, the publisher posts to real accounts, and view data feeds back into the scorer.
deploy: Pipeline on the agent with subagent fan-out, run log and clip scores in Convex, creator veto pages on Cloudflare Pages, clips published to a real creator's social accounts.
proof: Top clips actually posted to a real podcast's account during the event, with the run log to show for it.
score: The bar is published, not rendered; judges open the live social post and the pipeline log side by side.
scenario: As an indie podcaster in Kochi with 40 episodes and zero clips, I drop episode 41 at 1pm. The crew argues over 9 candidate moments, ships the top 3 with captions and thumbnails, and posts them to my Instagram by 4pm. The best clip is a tangent I would never have picked, and it beats my last 5 posts.
why: The pipeline is honestly multi-agent: scoring is a debate, cutting is fan-out, and the judge panel before publish is the observability judges want. Most teams will render clips and stop; posting to a real account during the event is the whole track. Recruit a podcaster early.
need: Manager pipeline: transcriber, moment scorer, fan-out cutters, captioner, artist, publisher
In-crew judge panel scores every candidate hook before publish, with scores logged
Real surface: the publisher posts top clips to a consenting creator's actual account
Run log in Convex: per-clip scores, agent handoffs, and publish receipts
Creator veto pages on Cloudflare Pages to approve clips before posting
Memory holds the show's voice, banned topics, and past winners
Feedback loop: early view counts re-rank what the scorer looks for next episode
levelups: Remembers you: the crew keeps the show's voice, in-jokes, and what flopped, so episode two clips get smarter. L4: it avoids repeating a flopped format unprompted. L5: wipe memory and it edits like a stranger.

Learns from use: view and completion data on published clips retrain the scorer. L4: engagement flows back and re-ranks hooks automatically. L5: show scorer picks converging with actual winners across episodes.
